content:
Cafe at the centre of a national security case, Leave Bookstore (留下書舍), which has been closed for over a month, announced today (the 25th) that it will proceed with its original plan to cease operations after 30 August. The bookstore will reopen for its final five days of business — from tomorrow (the 26th) through Sunday (the 30th), from 1pm to 9pm daily — clearing stock in a clearance sale.

Leave Bookstore posted a farewell message on social media, writing: 'Four years pass in the blink of an eye; though the flowers fall, friends remain. In books there is no golden house, no beauty fair. Why force the unfulfilled ambitions of a lifetime? Boiling wine and sharing joy is enough. Facing this final note I weep, not knowing what to say, only a word of thanks. Take care.'

Founded four years ago, Leave Bookstore announced last month it would close at the end of August. Just one day later, national security police visited and arrested three people from the bookstore on suspicion of committing sedition under Article 23. The same case also involved two arrests connected to Garden Books (田園書屋). Garden Books, with a 50-year history, also announced at the end of last month that it would close upon the expiry of its lease. The publication allegedly involved in the case is said to be 'The Red Flowers of Today Blooming: Identity and Belonging in the Era of Xi Jinping', written by Chinese-American journalist Elaine Chao (馮哲芸).

Leave Bookstore was founded in 2022 by veteran journalist Shum Wan-wah (岑蘊華) and several former reporters from Stand News (立場新聞). By that time, Apple Daily (蘋果日報), Stand News and Citizen News (眾新聞) had already ceased operations one after another. The name 'Leave Bookstore' (留下書舍) was chosen to signify 'leaving behind writing'. The store specialised in books related to journalism and the media, and frequently hosted talks and author sharing sessions.

On the 14th of last month, Leave Bookstore announced it would close on 30 August, citing 'unclear red lines' as one of the reasons for its closure.
